title: Beyond elevation: climate, geography, and the diversification of Himalayan Rhododendrons. A commentary on ‘Phenotypic and genetic variation among Rhododendron arboreum species complex widely distributed throughout the Himalayas suggests an obscure geographic origin of the clade’
content: The Himalaya is among the world's most remarkable natural laboratories of evolution. Extreme elevational gradients, sharp climatic transitions, repeated glacial oscillations and highly fragmented landscapes have generated one of the richest mountain floras on Earth (Manish and Pandit, 2018; Rana et al., 2019). Yet despite a long history of botanical exploration, Himalayan plant science has remained disproportionately focused on taxonomy, floristics and biogeography, with comparatively fewer studies examining the ecological and evolutionary processes underlying diversification. Thus, the processes shaping plant evolution across Himalayan environmental gradients remain one of the central questions in mountain evolutionary biology. In this context, the study by Noshiro et al. (2026) represents an important contribution.
